\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اجرت} (ujrat)}{اجرت (ujrat)}]{\ur{اجرت} (ujrat) — wages; payment for work}

\label{lesson:UR-C495-ujrat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for dismissed from a job, then the Urdu for to recruit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اجرت}}
\textbf{\ur{اجرت}} — \emph{ujrat} — \textquotedblleft{}wages; payment for work\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مزدوروں} \ur{کو} \ur{ان} \ur{کی} \ur{اجرت} \ur{شام} \ur{کو} \ur{ملتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mazdūroṅ ko un kī ujrat shām ko miltī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The labourers get their wages in the evening.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اجرت}} (\emph{ujrat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ujra}, \textquotedblleft{}a wage, a fee\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ujrat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ujrat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mazdūroṅ ko un kī ujrat shām ko miltī hai.} — The labourers get their wages in the evening.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for dismissed from a job, then the Urdu for to recruit, then say \emph{ujrat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہڑتال} (haṛtāl)}{ہڑتال (haṛtāl)}]{\ur{ہڑتال} (haṛtāl) — a strike (stopping work)}

\label{lesson:UR-C495-hartal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to recruit, then the Urdu for wages.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہڑتال}}
\textbf{\ur{ہڑتال}} — \emph{haṛtāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a strike (stopping work)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کل} \ur{سے} \ur{کارخانے} \ur{میں} \ur{ہڑتال} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kal se kārkhāne meṅ haṛtāl hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There has been a strike at the factory since yesterday.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہڑتال}} (\emph{haṛtāl}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{haṛtāl}, \textquotedblleft{}closing shops in protest\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{haṭṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}a market\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13944).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

Before the new one: say the Urdu for wages, then the Urdu for a strike.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹھیکیدار} (ṭhekedār)}{ٹھیکیدار (ṭhekedār)}]{\ur{ٹھیکیدار} (ṭhekedār) — a contractor}

\label{lesson:UR-C495-thekedar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a strike, then the Urdu for expertise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹھیکیدار}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹھیکیدار}} — \emph{ṭhekedār} — \textquotedblleft{}a contractor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ٹھیکیدار} \ur{نے} \ur{مزدوروں} \ur{کو} \ur{جلدی} \ur{بلایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭhekedār ne mazdūroṅ ko jaldī bulāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The contractor called the labourers early.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹھیکیدار}} (\emph{ṭhekedār}) is built from \emph{ṭhekā}, \textquotedblleft{}a contract for piecework\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under \emph{*ṭhīkka}, \textquotedblleft{}firm, right\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5503), and the ending \emph{-dār}, usually traced to Persian \emph{-dār}, \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کھپانا} (khapānā)}{کھپانا (khapānā)}]{\ur{کھپانا} (khapānā) — to use up (time or effort); to toil over}

\label{lesson:UR-C495-khapana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for expertise, then the Urdu for a contractor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کھپانا}}
\textbf{\ur{کھپانا}} — \emph{khapānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to use up (time or effort); to toil over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{اس} \ur{کام} \ur{میں} \ur{دو} \ur{سال} \ur{کھپائے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne is kām meṅ do sāl khapāe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He spent two whole years toiling over this work.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کام} \ur{میں} \ur{تین} \ur{گھنٹے} \ur{کھپائے}, \emph{us ne kām meṅ tīn ghanṭe khapāe}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کھپانا}} (\emph{khapānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{khapānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to destroy\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{kṣapyatē}, \textquotedblleft{}is destroyed, is used up\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3655); CDIAL glosses it \textquotedblleft{}to destroy\textquotedblright{}, and the everyday sense \textquotedblleft{}to use up time or effort\textquotedblright{} is a later one it does not record.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khapānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khapānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{us ne is kām meṅ do sāl khapāe.} — He spent two whole years toiling over this work.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for expertise, then the Urdu for a contractor, then say \emph{khapānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
